A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FALCON and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–F. Relocated material can be matched reliably across versions.

before.justification: Sections 4–6 and Appendix D report original topology-classification, circuit-performance prediction, inverse-design, and held-out RVCO experiments using Cadence-simulated circuits.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical evaluations, updates prediction results, and adds five-seed evaluations and a synthesized DBAMixer example.

M1.justification: Section 5 changes the specified GNN from iterative edge-embedding updates and edge-sum pooling to node-state message passing with residual ReLU updates and node-mean pooling. This is a substantive architectural revision, not equivalent notation. Appendix D also introduces optional weighted and interval-constrained inference objectives.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same million-circuit dataset, five circuit families, 20 topologies, and 30 GHz setting. Held-out RVCO evaluation already appears in v1. The additional DBAMixer example belongs to existing coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version reports experimental comparisons against external competing methods. Appendix A retains the same qualitative comparison roster; its revised capability attributions do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The documented splits, metrics, training settings, approximately 30,000-example RVCO fine-tuning protocol, and 9,500-instance inverse-design evaluation retain their settings and thresholds. Additional seeds repeat existing evaluations. No experiments using the newly described alternative objectives are reported.

E4.justification: New Appendix C examines sensitivity to initialization and data shuffling, and Appendix E.5 adds a DBAMixer schematic/layout case study. The existing RVCO generalization analysis moves into Section 5; no new component ablation or broader distribution-shift evaluation is added.

E5.justification: V1 Appendix F.2 explicitly states that repeated training runs were not performed. V2 replaces this with five specified random seeds and mean scores with 95% confidence intervals for both topology selection and forward prediction in Appendix C, substantially expanding statistical support.

E6.justification: Reported GNN results are revised: full-test mean relative error changes from 9.14% to 9.09%, and RVCO zero-shot/fine-tuned errors change from 33.1%/0.8% to 30.4%/0.9%. These accompany the revised architecture specification, not an isolated same-model improvement. V2 adds seed-aggregate results and a DBAMixer example with 0.2% error. Classification accuracy and aggregate inverse-design success remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds mathematical definitions for weighted masked performance loss and penalties for lower, upper, or two-sided performance bounds. These extend the objective formulation. Existing passive-component derivations remain unchanged, and no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The principal claims about the integrated pipeline, large Cadence dataset, topology-selection accuracy, prediction error, sub-second inference, and unseen-topology adaptation retain their meaning. The added contribution bullet emphasizing CPU inference speed restates an existing claim.

C2.justification: Appendix F.2 explicitly distinguishes topology selection from novel-circuit generation, discusses restricted frequency generalization, and acknowledges that analytical layout models cannot replace EM simulation or post-layout verification and omit electromigration constraints. Appendix C adds interpretations of seed stability. These extend existing applicability qualifications without overturning the main conclusions.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly specifies scalar dummy node initialization and its linear projection, while dropping v1's explicit 256-unit decoder-width disclosure. Hardware, runtime information, data-generation details, layout constants, and code/data access statements otherwise remain substantially unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix A revises capability attributions, including RF/mm-wave support for Cao et al., BO-SPGP, and AutoCkt, GCN-RL code availability, and L2DC simulator fidelity. The Gilmer et al. message-passing citation is removed. The overall positioning and remaining cited literature are retained.

P1.justification: Graph-representation material and RVCO fine-tuning move from appendices into the main text. V2 reorganizes the corresponding appendices, rewrites the architecture and limitations passages, and adds explanatory cross-references. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds confidence-interval Tables 12–13 and the DBAMixer schematic/layout in Figure 15. It relocates v1 Figure 13 to main-text Figure 2 and v1 Table 11 to Table 3, with accompanying reflow and caption adjustments. Most existing displays retain their design.

improvement.justification: Five-seed confidence intervals replace v1's explicit absence of repeated training, strengthening evidence for the central ML results. Expanded frequency and physical-verification limitations improve transparency, and the new objective definitions improve technical specificity. These gains outweigh the lost decoder-width disclosure, but task coverage and aggregate end-to-end validation remain unchanged, supporting a limited overall improvement.
